text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Al McLean resigns as Speaker of the Ontario legislature: Embattled Member of Provincial Parliament avoids vote on ouster in wake of sexual harassment case.
- Toronto's smoking ban faces being scrapped: City councillors want debate reopened.
- Israeli troops, Palestinians clash: Violence triggered by decision to open archeological tunnel in Jerusalem.
- Ottawa to seek secession ruling: Request guaranteed to anger Quebec.
- Clinton administration promises fight over trade: 'Hell to pay' if Canada thinks ruling is final, Democrat says.
- U.S. publisher bids for Nelvana: Golden Books offers C$140-million for animation firm.
- Falconbridge chief Franklin Pickard dies: Collapses at company's copper site in northern Chile.
- Mortgage rates trimmed again: Quarter-point cut may boost home sales.
- Canada to lead G7 in growth, IMF says: Predicts economy will advance 3.2 percent.
- Service Corp International undeterred by Loewen's rejection: Analysts expect a higher bid from giant U.S. funeral operator.
- Mortgage rates fall, one-year now 5.95 percent.
- Golden Books bids C$140 million for strife-ridden Nelvana.
